pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 50 KB
pages.description: Shrink a one-page PDF to under 50 KB for strict form uploads like marksheets and certificates. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Some portals cap each document at 50 KB. A single page made from text fits easily; a single scanned page usually can too.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 50 KB
paragraphs: 50 KB is about the smallest limit you will see for a PDF, and it is realistic for one page. A page exported from Word or a web form is mostly text and is often already under it after the lossless cleanup.

A scanned page is a photo, so it has to shrink. We lower its resolution step by step, as far as 50 dpi for color and 100 dpi for black and white, and keep the first step that fits. Several scanned pages at 50 KB will usually hit that floor, and then you get the smallest file we could make with a note saying so.
tips: Upload one page per file. At this size every extra scanned page makes the rest blurrier.
Scan certificates and marksheets in black and white if the form accepts it. It is far smaller than color at the same sharpness.
If the scan is a phone photo, crop away the table or desk around the paper first.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 100 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 100 KB for exam, admission and government forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Exam and admission forms often cap certificates and ID scans at 100 KB. Scanned pages are mostly image data, so they usually get there with text still readable.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 100 KB
paragraphs: 100 KB is tight, but it depends on what is in the file. A PDF made straight from a document, exported from Word or a web form, is mostly text, and text takes almost no space. Those usually fit after the lossless pass alone. Scanned pages are photos of paper, and those are what have to shrink.

For scans we lower the resolution of the page images one step at a time, down to 50 dpi at the lowest setting, and stop at the first step that fits. Anything drawn as real text stays sharp at every step; only images lose detail.
tips: Scan one page per file if the form allows it. Every scanned page adds to the size.
Scan in grayscale or black and white when color does not matter. It compresses far better than color.
Crop the scan to the edge of the document. A strip of scanner lid still costs bytes.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 150 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 150 KB for scholarship, admission and registration forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 150 KB is a common cap for certificates and ID proofs on registration portals. Two or three scanned pages usually fit.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 150 KB
paragraphs: Registration and scholarship portals often allow 150 KB per document: an ID proof, a caste or income certificate, a fee receipt. Two or three scanned pages usually fit with the text still easy to read.

We run a lossless cleanup first, then step the page images down in resolution and JPEG quality together until the file is under 150,000 bytes. We stop at the first step that fits, so nothing is squeezed harder than it needs to be.
tips: Front and back of an ID card fit comfortably on one page. Put them side by side before scanning.
Check stamps, seals and signatures in the result. Fine, faint marks are the first thing to blur.
If the portal asks for a PDF but you have a photo, convert it to PDF first, then compress it here.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 200 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 200 KB for visa, ID and application uploads. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 200 KB is a common limit on visa and ID document uploads. A one or two page scan usually fits with room to spare.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 200 KB
paragraphs: Visa and ID portals often ask for a passport page, a bank statement or a photo ID under 200 KB. A one or two page scan usually gets there at a resolution that is still easy to read.

We try a lossless cleanup first. If the file is still too big, we step the page images down in resolution and JPEG quality together and keep the gentlest step that fits under 200,000 bytes, so it passes however the portal counts a kilobyte.
tips: Zoom in on the result before you upload. Small print like passport numbers and dates is what suffers first.
If a long statement will not fit, check whether the portal only needs the pages it asks for.
Filling in a form PDF? Fill it and save it first. The stronger settings can flatten fillable fields.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 300 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 300 KB for online application portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 300 KB leaves enough room for a few scanned pages at a size that is still comfortable to read on screen.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 300 KB
paragraphs: At 300 KB there is room for a few scanned pages at a resolution that reads comfortably on screen, or a much longer document if it was created digitally.

Digital PDFs mostly shrink in the lossless pass: we repack the file's internal structure and drop parts nothing uses, without changing how anything looks. Scans shrink by lowering image resolution a step at a time until the file fits.
tips: Include only the pages you need. Each extra scanned page counts against the limit.
If you can rescan, 150 to 200 dpi is plenty for reading on screen and leaves far less to compress away than 600 dpi.
If a file cannot reach 300 KB, you get the smallest version we could make and a note saying so.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 400 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 400 KB for application and document verification portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 400 KB leaves room for several scanned pages at a comfortable resolution, which is what most verification portals need.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 400 KB
paragraphs: At 400 KB a short scanned document, like a four or five page transcript or a lease, usually fits at around 100 to 150 dpi. That is sharp enough to read small print on screen.

Documents with photos or colored backgrounds are the harder case, because every page is a full-color image. Those step down further, and the result is the gentlest setting that still fits under 400,000 bytes.
tips: Remove blank pages, including the backs of single-sided sheets that a duplex scanner picked up.
A document created on a computer, rather than scanned, is often already far under 400 KB. Try the original file before a scan of a printout.
Zoom in to 100% on the result and read one line of small print before you upload it.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 500 KB for applications, certificates and forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 500 KB fits most multi-page scans, like transcripts or a set of certificates, without the pages turning blurry.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 500 KB
paragraphs: 500 KB fits most multi-page documents: transcripts, a set of certificates, a signed contract. Pages usually stay close to print quality.
Our highest-quality settings keep color images at 200 to 300 dpi. We only go lower when the file still does not fit, and we always stop at the first setting that does.
tips: Photos embedded in a document are usually most of its size. Text and tables add very little.
Keep your original for printing. The compressed copy is meant for uploading.
Password-protected PDFs cannot be compressed. Remove the password first, then upload.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 1 MB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 1 MB for job applications and resume uploads. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Job sites and applicant tracking systems often limit resumes and cover letters to 1 MB. Text-heavy PDFs usually fit without visible change.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 1 MB
paragraphs: Job sites and applicant tracking systems often cap resumes, cover letters and portfolios at 1 MB. A resume exported from Word or Google Docs is usually well under that already. Oversized ones are almost always carrying a large photo or come from a design tool.
Text and vector graphics stay sharp at every setting. Only embedded images are resampled, so a headshot or logo gets smaller while your text stays crisp.
tips: PDFs exported from design tools often embed images at full resolution, which is exactly what we reduce.
Keep your text as real text rather than a scanned image, so applicant tracking systems can read it.
The download is named yourfile.fit.pdf. Rename it to something like firstname-lastname-resume.pdf before you apply.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 2 MB
pages.description: Shrink a PDF to under 2 MB for upload forms and portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 2 MB is a common ceiling on upload forms. Photos inside the PDF get resized just enough to fit and no further.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 2 MB
paragraphs: 2 MB is a common ceiling on upload forms, insurance claims and school portals. Photo-heavy PDFs and long scans are the usual reasons a file goes over.
We reduce the photos inside the PDF only as far as needed. The first setting keeps images at 300 dpi and high JPEG quality, and the search stops at the first setting that fits.
tips: Phone photos dropped into a document can be several megabytes each on their own.
If the form accepts more than one file, splitting a long document keeps each part sharper.
The original is deleted 5 minutes after the run finishes, so try other sizes before then.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 5 MB
pages.description: Shrink a large PDF to under 5 MB for email attachments and portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: For big scans and photo-heavy reports that need to go through email or a portal with a 5 MB cap.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 5 MB
paragraphs: 5 MB covers most email attachments and portals with a larger limit. Big scans, photo reports and slide decks saved as PDF are the files that usually need it.
At this size most files keep high-resolution images. Very large ones, like dozens of scanned pages or print-resolution artwork, may still need the stronger settings.
tips: Uploads can be up to 50 MB. Split anything larger before you start.
Big files take longer, since each setting is a full pass over the document. A large scan can take a minute or two.
Keep your original. The compressed copy is for sending, not for printing or editing.

pages.heading: Compress a PDF to 10 MB
pages.description: Shrink a large PDF to under 10 MB for email, court filings and grant or tender portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: For long scans, portfolios and reports that need to get under a 10 MB email or portal limit without losing print quality.

guide.title: Getting a PDF under 10 MB
paragraphs: 10 MB is the limit for many email systems, e-filing portals and grant or tender submissions. The files that need it are usually long scans, design portfolios or reports full of photos.

At this size most documents keep images at 200 to 300 dpi, which still prints well. Often the lossless pass alone gets there, since PDFs exported from design tools tend to carry duplicate fonts and uncompressed data.
tips: Uploads can be up to 50 MB. Split anything larger into parts first.
Some mail servers count an attachment after encoding, which makes it about a third bigger. If a 10 MB mail limit rejects the file, try a 7 MB target.
Large files take longer, since each setting is a full pass over the document. Leave the tab open until it finishes.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 20 KB
pages.description: Shrink a signature or photo to under 20 KB for online application forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Signature uploads on application forms are often capped at 10 to 20 KB. A signature on a plain background compresses very well.

guide.title: Getting a signature or small image under 20 KB
paragraphs: Application forms often want a scanned signature between 10 and 20 KB. A signature is dark ink on a plain background, which compresses very well once the image is a sensible size.
We shrink the pixel dimensions and JPEG quality together, down to 800 pixels on the longest side at the smallest setting, and keep the gentlest step that fits under 20,000 bytes.
tips: Sign in dark ink on plain white paper, and crop tightly around the signature before uploading.
Take the photo in good light so the paper comes out white rather than gray. A clean background takes far fewer bytes.
If the form also asks for exact pixel dimensions, check them. We shrink to hit the file size, not to a specific width and height.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 50 KB
pages.description: Shrink a passport-style photo to under 50 KB for application forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Photo uploads on application forms are often limited to 50 KB. A phone photo gets resized and re-encoded until it fits.

guide.title: Getting a photo under 50 KB
paragraphs: Photo uploads for exam registrations, applications and ID cards are often limited to 50 KB. A phone photo is usually several megabytes, so it has to lose most of its pixels.
We scale the photo down and lower JPEG quality together until it fits. Even the smallest setting keeps 800 pixels on the longest side, which is more than most photo forms display.
tips: Crop to head and shoulders before uploading. Fewer pixels to start with means less detail has to go.
Use a plain, light background. It takes far fewer bytes than a busy one.
If the form also has a minimum size or exact pixel dimensions, check the result against them. We aim for the file size only.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 100 KB
pages.description: Shrink a JPG, PNG or photo to under 100 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 100 KB keeps a photo sharp enough for a profile picture or an ID upload.

guide.title: Getting an image under 100 KB
paragraphs: 100 KB is enough for a clear profile picture, an ID photo or a photo of a document for most online forms.
For a JPEG we first try an optimized re-encode that keeps every pixel exactly as it is. If that is not enough, we reduce the dimensions and quality step by step until it fits.
tips: A PNG comes back as a PNG, with its transparency kept.
Photographing a document? Shoot it flat and in good light, filling the frame. Less background means more detail survives.
We keep your image's shape and never crop it, so crop first if the form wants a particular framing.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 150 KB
pages.description: Shrink a photo to under 150 KB for profile pictures, ID uploads and online forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 150 KB is plenty for a clear profile or ID photo. A phone photo gets resized and re-encoded until it fits.

guide.title: Getting a photo under 150 KB
paragraphs: Profile pictures, student and employee ID uploads, and many online forms cap photos at 150 KB. That is enough for a clear, sharp picture at the size these sites display it.
We resize and re-encode in steps, from 4000 pixels on the longest side down to 800, and keep the largest, highest-quality step that fits under 150,000 bytes.
tips: Crop to the part of the photo that matters first. Every pixel you remove is one less that has to be squeezed.
Photos with lots of fine detail, like foliage or patterned clothes, take more bytes than a plain background.
A JPEG comes back as a JPEG and a PNG as a PNG, so the file type the form asked for is kept.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 200 KB
pages.description: Shrink a photo or scanned image to under 200 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 200 KB is enough for a clear photo of a document or a good-quality portrait.

guide.title: Getting an image under 200 KB
paragraphs: 200 KB leaves room for a sharp portrait, a readable photo of a certificate or a product image for a listing.
We stop at the first setting that fits, so an image that only needs a little squeezing keeps most of its resolution and detail.
tips: iPhone photos (HEIC) work too. HEIC photos are saved as JPEG.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location. It saves space and keeps where you took the photo private.
Every file comes back in the format you uploaded: a PNG stays a PNG, a WebP a WebP.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 300 KB
pages.description: Shrink a photo or scanned document image to under 300 KB for application portals. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 300 KB is a common cap for document photos on application portals. Text in a photographed page stays readable at this size.

guide.title: Getting an image under 300 KB
paragraphs: Many portals ask for a photo of a document, like an ID card, a utility bill or a receipt, under 300 KB. At this size a photographed page usually keeps 1600 pixels or more on its longest side, which keeps printed text readable.
We first try an optimised re-encode that leaves the pixels untouched. If that is not enough, we lower dimensions and JPEG quality together and stop at the first step that fits.
tips: Photograph documents flat, from straight above, in daylight. Shadows and a tilted page cost bytes and readability.
Crop out the background around the document before uploading.
Screenshots saved as PNG often drop far below 300 KB once converted, since PNG stores every pixel without lossy compression.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink a large phone photo to under 500 KB without it looking compressed. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Phone photos are often 3 to 5 MB. At 500 KB they still look good on any screen.

guide.title: Getting an image under 500 KB
paragraphs: Phone photos are often 3 to 5 MB. At 500 KB they still look good on any screen, which is why it is a common limit for listings, profile uploads and support forms.
Our highest-quality setting keeps up to 4000 pixels on the longest side at JPEG quality 92. We only step down as far as the size requires.
tips: Most screens show far fewer pixels than a phone camera captures, so the size drop is rarely visible.
Large PNG screenshots often shrink the most, since they are stored without lossy compression.
Need several photos done? Each file is compressed separately; upload them one at a time.

pages.heading: Compress a JPG to 1 MB
pages.description: Shrink a high-resolution photo to under 1 MB for listings, portfolios and support forms. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Modern phone and camera photos are often 5 MB or more. Under 1 MB they still look sharp full screen.

guide.title: Getting a photo under 1 MB
paragraphs: A photo from a recent phone or camera is often 5 to 12 MB. Marketplaces, rental listings, portfolio sites and support forms commonly cap uploads at 1 MB.

At 1 MB most photos keep 3000 pixels or more on the longest side at high JPEG quality, which is sharper than nearly any screen can show. Often the lossless re-encode, which only strips metadata, is enough on its own.
tips: Stripping metadata also removes the photo's GPS location, which is worth doing before you post it publicly.
iPhone photos (HEIC) work too. HEIC photos are saved as JPEG.
RAW files are not supported. Export a JPEG from your editor, then compress that.

pages.heading: Compress a PNG to 100 KB
pages.description: Shrink a PNG screenshot, logo or scan to under 100 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: PNGs are stored without lossy compression, so screenshots and scans are often ten times bigger than they need to be.

guide.title: Getting a PNG under 100 KB
paragraphs: PNG keeps every pixel exactly, which is why a single screenshot or scanned page saved as PNG can be several megabytes. The result here stays a PNG: we reduce it to 256 colours, which screenshots, logos and diagrams barely show, and make it smaller in pixels only as far as 100 KB needs.
We try it at full size first, then step the pixel dimensions down, keeping the largest PNG that fits under 100,000 bytes. Transparent areas stay transparent.
tips: Logos keep their transparency, so they still work on a coloured background.
Crop screenshots to the part you need. A full-screen capture of a 4K display is a lot of pixels to squeeze.
A photo saved as PNG has too many colours to shrink well this way. If the form accepts JPEG, save the photo as a JPEG first; photos get much smaller that way.

pages.heading: Compress a PNG to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink a large PNG, like a screenshot or design export, to under 500 KB. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Design exports and full-screen screenshots saved as PNG are often 3 to 10 MB. Reduced to 256 colours they usually fit under 500 KB, still a PNG and still sharp.

guide.title: Getting a PNG under 500 KB
paragraphs: A design export or a high-resolution screenshot saved as PNG is often 3 to 10 MB, because PNG never throws detail away. Most of that is colour precision nobody sees: reduced to 256 colours, the same image usually drops under 500 KB and stays a PNG, with text as sharp as before.
We try it at full size first and make it smaller in pixels only if 500 KB needs that. Transparent areas stay transparent.
tips: Zoom in on small text in the result before you upload it, in case the image had to be made smaller in pixels to fit.
For a photo, export a JPEG from your design tool instead: photos shrink much better as JPEG than as PNG.
Images with large flat areas of one color, like diagrams, shrink the most.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG
pages.description: Convert an iPhone HEIC photo to JPG, and fit it under a size limit if you need one. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: iPhones save photos as HEIC. The US visa form (DS-160), UK passport photos and Canadian immigration uploads accept JPEG, not HEIC.

guide.title: Turning an iPhone photo into a JPG
paragraphs: iPhones save photos as HEIC to use less space. The US visa form (DS-160), UK passport photos and Canadian immigration uploads all ask for JPEG, and Windows needs a paid extension just to open a HEIC.

We convert it to a JPG, turned the right way up, with its colours converted to the standard sRGB every site expects, and keep every pixel when the limit allows. A JPG of the same photo is usually about twice the size of the HEIC, so if the form has a limit, pick it below and we fit the JPG under it in the same step.
tips: On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
To stop your iPhone saving HEIC at all, go to Settings, Camera, Formats and choose Most Compatible.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG under 1 MB
pages.description: Turn an iPhone HEIC photo into a JPG under 1 MB, in one step. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: An iPhone photo converted to JPG is often 3 to 6 MB. 1 MB still keeps plenty of detail.

guide.title: Getting an iPhone photo under 1 MB as a JPG
paragraphs: Converting a HEIC to JPG roughly doubles its size, so a photo that was 2 MB on your phone can land at 4 MB or more, over a 1 MB upload limit.

We convert and shrink in one step, keeping the most resolution that fits. A 12-megapixel iPhone photo under 1 MB usually keeps around 2,600 pixels on its long side, plenty for a form, a listing or a profile.
tips: On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
If the form also asks for exact pixel dimensions, open Exact size in pixels before you compress.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG under 200 KB
pages.description: Turn an iPhone HEIC photo into a JPG under 200 KB for an application form. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 200 KB is a common limit for photos on visa, exam and job application forms, which usually ask for JPEG.

guide.title: An iPhone photo as a JPG under 200 KB
paragraphs: Application forms that cap photos at 200 KB almost always want JPG too. Uploading the HEIC straight from a computer fails twice: wrong format, and several times too big.
We fix both at once. A 12-megapixel iPhone photo under 200 KB usually keeps around 1,800 pixels on its long side, still sharp for a portrait or a photo of a document.
tips: If the form gives exact pixel dimensions, like 600 x 600 for a US visa photo, open Exact size in pixels and enter them; we crop to fill.
On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: Convert HEIC to JPG under 100 KB
pages.description: Turn an iPhone HEIC photo into a JPG under 100 KB. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: 100 KB is tight for an iPhone photo: converted to JPEG at full size, one is often several megabytes.

guide.title: An iPhone photo as a JPG under 100 KB
paragraphs: At 100 KB there is no room for a full iPhone photo, so the pixel size has to come down as well as the quality. We step both down together and keep the first setting that fits, so it stays as sharp as that size allows.
A 12-megapixel iPhone photo under 100 KB usually keeps around 1,600 pixels on its long side, clear on screen and fine for most form previews.
tips: Crop to what the form needs before you upload, such as your face for an ID photo. Fewer pixels to keep means more quality for the ones left.
On an iPhone, uploading straight from Safari usually hands the site a JPG already. This is for HEIC files that have reached a computer, by AirDrop, iCloud or email.
We remove camera metadata such as GPS location from the JPG, which also keeps where you took the photo private.

pages.heading: US visa photo for the DS-160: 600 x 600, under 240 KB
pages.title: US visa photo (DS-160)
pages.description: Make your DS-160 visa photo a 600 x 600 pixel JPEG under 240 KB, as the U.S. Department of State requires. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The DS-160 takes a square JPEG, 600 x 600 pixels and no more than 240 KB. A phone photo is several megabytes and the wrong shape, so it gets cropped, resized and compressed in one go.

source.label: the U.S. Department of State's photo requirements

guide.title: Getting a DS-160 photo to 600 x 600 and under 240 KB
paragraphs: The State Department sets four technical rules for the digital photo: JPEG format, 240 KB or less, a square shape, and 600 x 600 pixels. A file that misses any of them cannot be uploaded.

This page is set up for all four. Your photo is cropped to a square, where you place the crop box, scaled to exactly 600 x 600 pixels and saved as a JPEG at the highest quality that stays under 240 KB. At that size a photo usually fits with room to spare, so very little quality is lost.
tips: If your head is not in the middle of the photo, drag the crop box over it before you press Compress.
The picture itself has rules too, such as the background, your expression and glasses. Check them on the State Department page before you take it.
If the upload still complains, check that it is a JPEG. A PNG or HEIC from a phone is converted here, but a renamed file is not.

faq.q: How big should my head be in a 600 x 600 DS-160 photo?
faq.a: The State Department wants your head, measured from the bottom of the chin to the top of the head, to take up 50% to 69% of the photo's height. In a 600 x 600 image that is about 300 to 414 pixels. Place the crop box here so your head fills that share before you compress.

faq.q: Can I wear glasses in my US visa photo?
faq.a: No, in most cases. Eyeglasses are no longer allowed in new visa photos. The only exception is when they cannot be removed for medical reasons, such as after eye surgery, and then you must provide a medical statement signed by a health professional. Take the glasses off before the photo is taken.

faq.q: Can this page make my DS-160 photo background white?
faq.a: No. This page crops, resizes and compresses the photo, and leaves the background as it is. The State Department asks for a plain white or off-white background and a photo taken within the last 6 months, so take a new photo against a white wall if yours does not meet that.

pages.heading: Indian e-Visa passport page: PDF under 300 KB
pages.title: Indian e-Visa passport page
pages.description: Compress the scanned bio page of your passport to a PDF under 300 KB for the Indian e-Visa application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The Indian e-Visa asks for the bio page of your passport as a PDF between 10 KB and 300 KB. A scan or phone photo of it is usually far bigger.

source.label: the Indian e-Visa site (Instructions for Applicant)

guide.title: Getting a passport page PDF under 300 KB
paragraphs: The e-Visa form takes the scanned bio page of your passport, the page with your photograph and details, as a PDF of at least 10 KB and at most 300 KB. Documents for a business or medical e-Visa have the same limits.

A single scanned page fits in 300 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text and your photo stay as sharp as the limit allows. The 10 KB minimum is never a problem for a real scan.
tips: Scan or photograph only the bio page, flat and in good light, with the whole page in the frame.
If your passport page is a JPG, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
Keep one page per file. The form asks for the bio page on its own.

faq.q: How long must my passport be valid for an Indian e-Visa?
faq.a: Your passport needs at least six months of validity on the day you apply, and at least two blank pages for the immigration officer's stamp. Check the expiry date printed on the bio page before you scan it, since that is the page you upload.

faq.q: What details must show on the passport page I upload for the e-Visa?
faq.a: Upload the photo page with your personal details readable: name, date of birth, nationality and expiry date. The site warns that an application may be rejected if uploaded documents are not clear. After compressing, open the PDF and zoom in to check that every line of text can still be read.

faq.q: What other documents does the Indian e-Visa ask for besides the passport?
faq.a: It depends on the visa type. An e-Business Visa asks for a copy of your business card, and an e-Medical Visa for a letter from the Indian hospital on its letterhead. These are PDFs with the same 10 KB to 300 KB limit, and every document must be in English.

pages.heading: Indian e-Visa photo: square JPEG under 1 MB
pages.title: Indian e-Visa photo
pages.description: Make your Indian e-Visa photo a square JPEG between 10 KB and 1 MB, as the e-Visa application requires. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The Indian e-Visa takes a JPEG photo between 10 KB and 1 MB whose height and width are equal. A phone photo is rarely square, so it is cropped to 1000 x 1000 pixels and compressed to fit.

source.label: the Indian e-Visa site (Instructions for Applicant)

guide.title: Getting an e-Visa photo square and under 1 MB
paragraphs: The e-Visa form asks for a JPEG of at least 10 KB and at most 1 MB, with equal height and width. It does not name a pixel size, so this page makes it 1000 x 1000: square, detailed, and comfortably under 1 MB.

The photo is cropped to a square where you place the crop box, resized, and saved at the highest JPEG quality that fits. To use another pixel size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.
tips: If your face is not in the middle, drag the crop box over it before you press Compress.
The form also asks for a full face, front view, eyes open, without glasses, on a plain light background, with no shadows and no border.
A photo taken for a printed visa is fine to use; photograph or scan it in good light.

faq.q: How should my face be framed in the Indian e-Visa photo?
faq.a: The form asks you to centre your head in the frame and show the full head, from the top of your hair to the bottom of your chin, facing the camera. When you place the crop box here, leave a little space above your hair so the top of your head is not cut off.

faq.q: Can I change my e-Visa photo after I submit the application?
faq.a: Check it carefully first, because you are responsible for the photo and details you submit. Submitted applications are checked, and if an image is not appropriate you may get an email asking you to re-upload it, usually within 24 hours. The re-upload option is at the bottom of the e-Visa page.

faq.q: Does the Indian e-Visa accept a PNG or HEIC photo?
faq.a: The form takes JPEG only. Because this page makes a JPEG at an exact pixel size, a PNG or HEIC you drop here comes out as a JPEG. If the result is under the 10 KB minimum, it is padded up to it with an invisible comment and the picture stays the same.

guide.title: Getting Passport Seva documents under 1 MB in total
paragraphs: When you apply for an Indian passport at an embassy or consulate, the Passport Seva applicant portal asks you to upload your documents yourself. The mission guidelines state that each document must be a PDF of at most 1 MB, and that the total of all uploaded documents should be no more than 1 MB. Up to 5 documents can be uploaded, including the photograph and signature, and up to 3 in Upload Supporting Documents.

Since the limit is shared, this page aims each document at 300 KB, so three supporting documents come to 900 KB. A scan of a page or two fits in 300 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text stays as readable as the limit allows.
tips: Uploading fewer documents? Pick a larger limit under Use a different limit, keeping the total under 1 MB.
If a document is a photo, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
The portal allows 12 upload attempts in all, so check each file's size here before you upload it.
Applying in India instead? The photograph is taken at the Passport Seva Kendra, so no photo upload is needed.

faq.q: Where do I upload documents on the Passport Seva portal for an embassy application?
faq.a: After you submit the form, choose Upload Supporting Documents from the pop-up, or open My Application, select the three-dot menu and pick Upload Supporting Documents. Then select the category and sub category, choose your PDF and click Upload. The portal confirms with "Document has been uploaded successfully!"

faq.q: What happens if I use up all 12 upload attempts on Passport Seva?
faq.a: The portal shows an error that no more documents can be uploaded, and the guidelines say that form should be ignored: you have to fill in and submit a new application. Deleting and re-uploading a file counts towards the 12, so compress each document to size before the first upload.

faq.q: What photo size do Indian embassies want for a passport application?
faq.a: The embassy guidelines ask for a colour photo of 630 x 810 pixels on a white background, with your face taking up 80 to 85% of it, unaltered by software. The photo and signature count among the 5 documents you can upload. This page is for the PDF documents.

guide.title: Getting an IBPS photo to 200 x 230 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: IBPS guidelines ask for the photograph at 200 x 230 pixels with a file size between 20 KB and 50 KB. The minimum matters too: at 200 x 230 pixels a good-quality JPEG is often only 15 KB or so, and the form turns it away as too small.

Here the photo is cropped to 200 x 230 where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 50 KB, and if that comes out under 20 KB it is padded up to it. The padding is an invisible comment inside the file, so the picture is exactly the same.
tips: Recent IBPS notifications also ask for a live photo taken during registration, besides this upload. Check the notification for your exam.
Use a recent photo, face centred, on a light background. If your face is off to one side, drag the crop box over it.
Each recruitment publishes its own notification. If a form states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: Can I wear glasses or religious headwear in my IBPS photo?
faq.a: Religious headwear is allowed as long as it does not cover your face. Caps, hats and dark glasses are not accepted. If you wear ordinary glasses, make sure there are no reflections and your eyes can be clearly seen, and take the photo against a light-coloured, preferably white, background.

faq.q: Why won't the IBPS form let me go past the photo upload?
faq.a: The IBPS form does not let you move to the next stage until the photograph and signature meet the specifications, and it shows an error message if the file size or format is wrong. The photo must be a JPG or JPEG between 20 KB and 50 KB, so a file under 20 KB is refused as well as one over 50 KB.

faq.q: What happens if I upload my IBPS photo in the wrong place?
faq.a: IBPS says that if the photo is not uploaded in the photo space and the signature in the signature space, you will not be allowed to appear for the exam. Check the preview after uploading. You can edit the application and re-upload the photo, but only before you submit the online form.

source.label: IBPS guidelines for scanning and uploading documents

guide.title: Getting an IBPS signature to 140 x 60 and 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: IBPS guidelines ask for the signature at 140 x 60 pixels with a file size between 10 KB and 20 KB. A signature at 140 x 60 pixels is a tiny image, usually 3 to 5 KB even at the best quality, which is under the minimum and gets refused.

Here the signature is cropped to 140 x 60 where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 20 KB, and padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file. The signature itself is exactly the same.
tips: Sign with a black pen on plain white paper, and photograph or scan it in good light.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
Each recruitment publishes its own notification. If a form states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: Can I sign in capital letters on the IBPS form?
faq.a: No. IBPS does not accept a signature in capital letters. Sign in your usual handwriting with a black ink pen on white paper. The signature has to be your own, made by you and not by any other person, and it should be clearly visible rather than smudged or blurred.

faq.q: Does my IBPS signature have to match the one I sign at the exam?
faq.a: Yes. At the exam you sign the attendance sheet or call letter, and if that signature does not match the one you uploaded, IBPS disqualifies you. Upload the signature you will actually use on exam day, signed the same way each time.

faq.q: What else do I upload with my signature on the IBPS form?
faq.a: Besides the signature, the IBPS form has separate upload links for your photograph, left thumb impression, handwritten declaration and your 10th standard (SSC/SSLC) certificate, plus a further certificate if one applies to you. The certificates go up as A4 PDFs of up to 500 KB. Your application is not registered until all of them are uploaded.

guide.title: Getting an SBI photo to 200 x 230 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks for a recent passport-style colour photo, 200 x 230 pixels preferred, with a file size between 20 KB and 50 KB, as a JPG or JPEG.

Here the photo is cropped to 200 x 230 where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 50 KB, and if that comes out under 20 KB it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file. The picture is exactly the same.
tips: Use a light, preferably white, background and look straight at the camera. Caps, hats and dark glasses are not accepted.
SBI also asks for a live photo taken with your webcam or phone during the application, besides this upload.
SBI publishes a notice for each recruitment. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What is the SBI clerk photo size in KB?
faq.a: For the Junior Associate (clerical cadre) recruitment, SBI asks for a recent passport-style colour photo of 4.5 cm x 3.5 cm, 200 x 230 pixels preferred, between 20 KB and 50 KB, as a JPG or JPEG. Here it is cropped to 200 x 230 and padded up to 20 KB if it comes out smaller.

faq.q: Do I need printed copies of my SBI application photo?
faq.a: Yes. SBI advises keeping about 8 copies of the same photo you upload, because they are needed later in the selection process. At the exam you bring your call letter with that photo pasted on it plus two more copies. Candidates without them are not allowed to appear.

faq.q: Can I change my photo after saving the SBI application?
faq.a: Yes, while the form is still open. When you save a partly filled form, SBI gives you a provisional registration number and password, and you can reopen and edit it three times only. If the photo is unclear you may re-upload it. Once you submit the completed application, no change is allowed.

guide.title: Getting an SBI signature to 140 x 60 and 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks for your signature in black ink on white paper, 140 x 60 pixels preferred, with a file size between 10 KB and 20 KB.

A signature at 140 x 60 pixels is usually 3 to 5 KB even at the best quality, which is under the minimum. Here it is cropped where you place the crop box, saved at the best quality under 20 KB and padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file.
tips: Sign with a black pen on plain white paper, and photograph or scan it in good light.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
SBI publishes a notice for each recruitment. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: Will SBI accept a signature in capital letters?
faq.a: No. SBI's notice says a signature in capital letters is not accepted. Write it in black ink on white paper, the way you normally sign. It must be your own signature, signed by you and not by anyone else, and clearly visible in the uploaded image.

faq.q: What happens if my SBI exam signature looks different from my upload?
faq.a: On exam day you sign the attendance sheet or call letter at the centre. SBI's notice states that if that signature does not match the one uploaded with your application, you are disqualified, so upload the signature you will reproduce at the exam.

faq.q: How should I scan my signature for SBI?
faq.a: SBI suggests scanning at a minimum of 200 dpi in true colour, cropping to the edge of the signature, then cropping to the final size. Save it as JPG or JPEG, for example image01.jpg. If the size or format is wrong, the form shows an error message.

pages.title: SBI left thumb impression
pages.description: Resize your left thumb impression to 240 x 240 pixels and 20 KB to 50 KB for SBI recruitment applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: SBI applications ask for a left thumb impression of 240 x 240 pixels and between 20 KB and 50 KB. It is cropped square, compressed, and padded up to 20 KB if it comes out smaller.

guide.title: Getting a thumb impression to 240 x 240 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks for your left thumb impression in black or blue ink on white paper, 240 x 240 pixels preferred, with a file size between 20 KB and 50 KB, as a JPG or JPEG.

Here the image is cropped square where you place the crop box, resized to 240 x 240, saved at the best quality under 50 KB, and padded up to 20 KB with an invisible comment inside the file if it comes out smaller.
tips: Press the thumb once, firmly and evenly, so the ridges are clear rather than a smudge.
Photograph it straight on in good light and crop close around the print first, so the square crop keeps all of it.
If you do not have a left thumb, the notice allows your right thumb.

faq.q: What is the SBI left thumb impression size in cm?
faq.a: SBI asks for 240 x 240 pixels at 200 DPI, which it states as 3 cm x 3 cm, between 20 KB and 50 KB, as a JPG or JPEG. Here the image is cropped square to 240 x 240 and padded up to 20 KB if it comes out under the minimum.

faq.q: Does SBI check my thumb impression at the exam?
faq.a: SBI may capture your thumb impression or iris digitally at various stages for biometric verification, and any inconsistency leads to rejection of your candidature. The notice advises against applying mehandi, ink or chemicals on your hands, so the thumb you upload should be the one you can present later.

faq.q: What if my uploaded SBI thumb impression is smudged?
faq.a: SBI says an unclear or smudged thumb impression may get your application rejected. After uploading, check the preview. If the print is not prominently visible, you can edit the application and upload a clearer image. Your application is not registered until the thumb impression is uploaded as specified.

pages.title: SBI handwritten declaration
pages.description: Resize your handwritten declaration to 800 x 400 pixels and 50 KB to 100 KB for SBI recruitment applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.

guide.title: Getting the declaration to 800 x 400 and 50 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: SBI's recruitment notice asks you to write the declaration in English, in black ink on white paper, and upload it at 800 x 400 pixels preferred, with a file size between 50 KB and 100 KB, as a JPG or JPEG. The notice gives the exact wording to copy.

Here the photo of your page is cropped where you place the crop box to the 2 to 1 shape of 800 x 400, saved at the best quality under 100 KB, and padded up to 50 KB with an invisible comment inside the file if it comes out smaller.
tips: Write the declaration in your own handwriting, not in capital letters, and copy the wording from the notice exactly.
Take the photo close around the text, then drag the crop box so it keeps every line.
SBI publishes a notice for each recruitment. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What do I write in the SBI handwritten declaration?
faq.a: You write your name and date of birth, declare that the information in your application is correct, true and valid, promise to present supporting documents when required, and state that the signature, photograph and left thumb impression are yours. The IBPS declaration has no date of birth or that last line, so copy SBI's wording from the notice.

faq.q: What size is the SBI handwritten declaration in cm?
faq.a: SBI asks for 800 x 400 pixels at 200 DPI, which it gives as 10 cm wide and 5 cm high, with a file size of 50 KB to 100 KB. Here your page is cropped to that 2 to 1 shape and padded up to 50 KB if it comes out smaller.

faq.q: Can I upload the SBI declaration as a PDF?
faq.a: No. SBI wants the declaration as a JPG or JPEG image, like the photo and signature. If your phone saves photos as HEIC, or you have a PNG, this page saves the 800 x 400 result as a JPEG, because the form asks for JPEG at that exact size.

pages.heading: RRB signature: 30 KB to 49 KB, at least 140 x 60 pixels
pages.title: RRB signature
pages.description: Resize your signature to 30 KB to 49 KB for Railway Recruitment Board applications (CEN 09/2025). Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: RRB's CEN 09/2025 asks for a signature JPEG between 30 KB and 49 KB, at least 140 x 60 pixels. A clean signature is far smaller than 30 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting an RRB signature to 30 KB to 49 KB
paragraphs: RRB's Centralised Employment Notification 09/2025 asks for a scanned signature, in running handwriting in black ink on white paper, as a JPG or JPEG between 30 KB and 49 KB and at least 140 x 60 pixels.

The form places the signature in a 35 x 20 mm box, so this page makes it 350 x 200 pixels, the same shape and well above the minimum. It is saved at the best quality under 49 KB, and because a signature at that size is usually well under 30 KB, it is padded up to 30 KB with an invisible comment inside the file. The signature is exactly the same.
tips: Sign in running (joined-up) handwriting. The notice rejects block, capital or disjointed letters.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
Each notification sets its own rules. The RRB photo is captured live in the application, so there is no photo to upload.

faq.q: Why would RRB reject my signature?
faq.a: CEN 09/2025 lists the grounds: a non-white background, ink other than black, block or capital letters, poor resolution or an unclear image, a signature that is partly cut off, a blank, a thumb impression instead of a signature, or someone else's signature. A rejection can happen at any stage of recruitment.

faq.q: Where do I sign again after the RRB application?
faq.a: Your signature must match the ones taken at the exams, document verification, the medical examination and appointment. At the CBT you write a self-declaration, sign and put your left thumb impression on the e-call letter in front of the invigilator. Signing in capital letters there is rejected too.

faq.q: Do I upload my RRB signature again before document verification?
faq.a: RRB advises candidates shortlisted for document verification to upload scanned copies of their photo and signature in true colour before their DV date, through the portal oirms-ir.gov.in/rrbdv. For the application itself, scan the signed paper at a minimum of 100 DPI.

pages.blurb: RRB's CEN 09/2025 asks SC/ST candidates who want the free travel pass to upload their certificate as a PDF under 400 KB. A scan is often bigger, so it is compressed until it fits.

guide.title: Getting an SC/ST certificate PDF under 400 KB
paragraphs: RRB's Centralised Employment Notification 09/2025 asks SC/ST candidates who want the free railway travel pass to upload their SC/ST certificate as a PDF of less than 400 KB, legible and clear.
A certificate of one or two pages fits in 400 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text stays as readable as the limit allows.
tips: Scan the certificate flat and in good light, with the whole page in the frame.
If your certificate is a photo, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
The certificate must be the latest valid one as on the closing date of the application.

faq.q: Do all SC/ST candidates upload a certificate on the RRB form?
faq.a: Only SC and ST candidates who want the free railway travel pass upload it. The pass is a free sleeper class pass, given with your e-call letter for the CBT, PET, document verification and medical examination as applicable, based on the caste certificate details in your online application.

faq.q: How do I use the RRB free travel pass on the train?
faq.a: Your e-call letter contains the travel authority. Book the reservation by giving a self-attested photocopy of the e-call letter and your SC/ST certificate at the ticket counter. On the journey carry your original community certificate and an original proof of identity, or you are treated as travelling without a ticket.

faq.q: Which SC/ST certificate format does RRB accept?
faq.a: CEN 09/2025 gives the format of the caste certificate for SC/ST candidates in Annexure-I. For the upload it must be a PDF only. At document verification, certificates must be in English or Hindi, and others need a self-attested translation. Misuse of the free travel facility can lead to rejection of your candidature.

pages.blurb: SSC asks for a scanned signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 20 KB, about 6.0 x 2.0 cm, in every current exam notice. A clean signature is often under 10 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting an SSC signature to 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: SSC's current notices set the same rule for the signature: a scanned signature in JPEG format, between 10 KB and 20 KB, about 6.0 cm wide and 2.0 cm high. That covers CGL, CHSL, MTS, Constable (GD), Junior Engineer, Stenographer, Selection Posts and the Sub-Inspector (CPO) exam.

The Constable (GD) 2026 notice adds a resolution of 300 DPI, which makes 6.0 x 2.0 cm come to 709 x 236 pixels. This page crops the signature to that size where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 20 KB. If that comes out under 10 KB it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file, so the signature is exactly the same.
tips: Sign on plain white paper and take the photo close around the signature, so it fills the crop box.
Your photograph is not uploaded: the application form captures it live with your camera while you fill it in.
Each SSC notice sets its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: Why does SSC reject a signature as blurred or miniature?
faq.a: SSC rejects applications summarily if the signature is blurred or miniature, or does not meet the rule of a JPEG of 10 KB to 20 KB, about 6.0 x 2.0 cm. The exception is candidates who opted for Aadhaar-based authentication, whose applications are not rejected on this ground.

faq.q: Is the SSC CHSL signature 6 x 2 cm or 4 x 2 cm?
faq.a: The CHSL 2026 notice gives both. Paragraph 9.6 says about 6.0 cm x 2.0 cm, while the application instructions later say about 4.0 cm x 2.0 cm. Both ask for a JPEG of 10 KB to 20 KB. This page uses 6.0 x 2.0 cm; for 4.0 x 2.0 cm, change it under Change size or pixels.

faq.q: Can I change my SSC signature after submitting the form?
faq.a: Check it first through the Preview or Print option, since SSC asks you to confirm the photograph and signature meet the requirements before submitting. After you submit the corrected or final application, or the correction window closes, no change is allowed, and requests by post or email are rejected.

pages.heading: UPSC photo for CSE, NDA, CDS, CAPF and other exams: JPEG, 20 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: UPSC photo (CSE, NDA, CDS, CAPF)
pages.description: Compress your photo to a JPEG between 20 KB and 200 KB for the UPSC application: CSE, NDA, CDS, CAPF, CMS, ESE and more. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: UPSC's application portal takes the photograph as a JPEG between 20 KB and 200 KB, the same for every exam. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed to fit.

source.label: UPSC's instructions for uploading the photo and signature

guide.title: Getting a UPSC photo to 20 KB to 200 KB
paragraphs: UPSC now takes one photo for all its exams. You upload it once in the Common Application Form on upsconline.nic.in, and it is used for the Civil Services, NDA, CDS, CAPF, CMS, ESE and the rest. The instructions ask for a passport-size colour photo as a JPEG between 20 KB and 200 KB, on a plain white background, with your face covering at least 75% of the photo and both ear lobes visible.

UPSC sets no pixel size, so this page keeps the photo as large as fits under 200 KB. It reduces the size step by step and stops at the first step that fits. If the result comes out under 20 KB, it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file, so the photo is exactly the same.
tips: Crop close around your head and shoulders before you upload, so your face fills at least 75% of the frame.
Don't sign the photo, and don't use one in uniform: the instructions refuse both.
The form also takes a live photo with your webcam or phone, and it must match this one. Use a recent photo that looks like you today.
The instructions ask for the file to be named photo, so save it as photo.jpg before you upload it.

faq.q: Can I wear glasses in my UPSC photo?
faq.a: UPSC does not accept a photo with your eyes hidden under coloured or dark glasses. Ordinary glasses are not on the refused list, but the instructions ask you to avoid glare on them, keep your eyes open and not covered by hair, and have no shadows on your face or the background.

faq.q: How does the UPSC live photograph work, and what if it does not match?
faq.a: Every UPSC application needs a live photo taken during the form, either with your device's webcam or by scanning a QR code on screen with your phone. It is matched against the passport-size photo you upload. If the two do not match, you are not allowed to go further with the application.

faq.q: Why does UPSC reject my photo?
faq.a: UPSC's sample photos show the reasons it rejects one: the face covers less than three quarters of the photo, the face is not looking straight at the camera or is misaligned, the photo is blurred, or the face is so close that it goes out of frame and the ear lobes are hidden. A grin, frown or raised eyebrows also goes against the instructions.

source.label: UPSC's instructions for uploading the photo and signature

guide.title: Getting the UPSC signature to 20 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: UPSC's instructions ask you to sign three times on plain white paper in black ink, one signature below the other, and to scan all three as a single image. The file is a JPEG between 20 KB and 100 KB, and the image dimensions are given as 350 to 500 pixels, without saying whether that is the width or the height.

This page crops the image to 450 x 500 pixels where you place the crop box, so both sides fall in that range whichever one is checked. It saves it at the best quality under 100 KB, and if that comes out under 20 KB it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file. The signatures are exactly the same.
tips: Leave a little space between the three signatures and keep them about the same width, so all three fit in the crop box.
Take the photo straight on, close around the signatures, in good light without shadows.
The instructions ask for the file to be named signature, so save it as signature.jpg before you upload it.

faq.q: Why does UPSC reject my signature image?
faq.a: UPSC checks that the image is clear, sharp and well lit, holds exactly three signatures one below the other, and is not rotated or upside down. The instructions say applications with a signature file that does not meet the specifications will be rejected, so check the image before you upload it.

faq.q: Can I sign on ruled or coloured paper for the UPSC form?
faq.a: No. UPSC asks for plain white paper with no lines or colours, and black ink. If your only paper is ruled, use a blank sheet instead, because the lines stay in the photo of your signatures. This page does not remove lines or change the background.

faq.q: Does a scribe upload a signature in the UPSC form?
faq.a: Yes, for the EPFO examination. UPSC's document list includes the scribe's signature as a JPEG of 20 KB to 100 KB named scribe_signature, uploaded in the EPFO Examination section, along with the scribe's photo as a JPEG of 20 KB to 200 KB named scribe_photo.

pages.heading: UPSC documents: certificates as PDFs of 50 KB to 300 KB
pages.title: UPSC documents
pages.description: Compress your caste, EWS, disability, matriculation or name-change certificate to a PDF under 300 KB for the UPSC application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: UPSC's application portal takes certificates as PDFs between 50 KB and 300 KB. A scanned certificate is often several megabytes, so it is compressed to fit under 300 KB.

guide.title: Getting UPSC certificates under 300 KB
paragraphs: In the Common Application Form on upsconline.nic.in, the certificates you upload are PDFs between 50 KB and 300 KB. That covers the caste certificate (the EWS certificate goes in the same place), the disability certificate, the matriculation certificate and the name-change affidavit or gazette notification. The instructions say a document is not uploaded if any other file name, format or size is used.

We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits under 300 KB, so the text stays as readable as the limit allows. Real text in a PDF is never blurred, only scanned images. This page does not make a PDF bigger, so a file already under 50 KB stays as it is.
tips: Name each file as UPSC lists it: caste_certificate, disability_certificate, board_certificate or name_change.
A certificate downloaded as a PDF can be under 50 KB. If yours is, scan the printed certificate instead, which comes out larger.
The photo ID is uploaded as a JPEG between 20 KB and 200 KB, not as a PDF. The UPSC photo page fits that size too.

faq.q: Where in the UPSC form do I upload each certificate?
faq.a: Each certificate goes in its own profile of the Common Application Form: the name-change affidavit or gazette notification in the Identity Profile, the matriculation certificate in the Matriculation Profile, the caste certificate in the Social Category Profile, and the disability certificate in the Disability Profile.

faq.q: Which extra documents does the UPSC EPFO exam ask for?
faq.a: For the EPFO examination, UPSC also asks for your bachelor's marksheet and degree certificate, and where they apply, a writing extremity certificate and an age relaxation certificate. Each is a PDF of 50 KB to 300 KB, named bachelor_marksheet, bachelor_certificate, writing_extremity_certificate and age_relaxation_certificate.

faq.q: What size is the PwBD recommendation certificate for UPSC?
faq.a: The PwD or PwBD recommendation certificate is a PDF of 50 KB to 300 KB, uploaded in the Disability Profile next to the disability certificate. UPSC lists its file name as pw_recommendation, so rename the compressed PDF to that before you upload it.

pages.description: Resize your photo to 130 x 170 pixels and 20 KB to 50 KB for TNPSC One Time Registration and Group exam applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: TNPSC asks for the photograph as a JPEG of 3.5 x 4.5 cm (130 x 170 pixels) between 20 KB and 50 KB, with your name and the date printed at the bottom. An image that small is only a few KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a TNPSC photo to 130 x 170 and 20 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: TNPSC's Instructions to Applicants ask for a colour studio photo on a white background, 4.5 cm high and 3.5 cm wide, which they give as 170 x 130 pixels. Your name and the date the photo was taken must be printed at the bottom, and the date must be on or after the date of the notification. The file is a JPEG between 20 KB and 50 KB, saved as Photograph.jpg.

This page crops the photo to 130 x 170 pixels where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 50 KB. A photo that small is usually under 20 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum with an invisible comment inside the file. The photo is exactly the same.
tips: Get the name and date printed on the photo at the studio. This page does not add text.
Place the crop box so it keeps the name and date strip at the bottom: TNPSC wants your face to take about 3 cm of the 4.5 cm height and the strip the rest.
TNPSC refuses selfies and phone photos, so upload a scan or the studio's digital copy.
Save the result as Photograph.jpg before you upload it.

faq.q: Can I reuse my TNPSC One Time Registration photo for a new application?
faq.a: For the One Time Registration, TNPSC asks for a photo taken within the last 3 months. Each online application then needs a photo taken on or after the date of that post's notification, so a photo from an earlier registration or application is too old once a new notification comes out.

faq.q: How do I upload a printed passport photo to TNPSC?
faq.a: If you only have a print, TNPSC says to paste it on plain white paper, scan it at 200 DPI, and crop the scan to show only the photograph. The whole sheet of paper must not be uploaded. On this page, place the crop box on the photo's edges, including the name and date strip.

faq.q: Where does my TNPSC photo appear at the exam?
faq.a: In the exam room you get a pre-printed OMR answer sheet with your photograph, name, register number and exam details on it, as in your hall ticket. Check the photo and details before you use the sheet, and tell the invigilator at once if anything is wrong, since a used sheet is not replaced.

pages.description: Resize your signature to 230 x 75 pixels and 10 KB to 20 KB for TNPSC One Time Registration and Group exam applications. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: TNPSC asks for the signature as a JPEG of 6.0 x 2.0 cm (230 x 75 pixels) between 10 KB and 20 KB. An image that small is only a few KB, so it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a TNPSC signature to 230 x 75 and 10 KB to 20 KB
paragraphs: TNPSC's Instructions to Applicants ask you to draw a box of 6.0 x 2.0 cm on white paper and sign inside it in blue or black ink. The image is cropped to just the box, which they give as 230 x 75 pixels, and saved as a JPEG between 10 KB and 20 KB named Signature.jpg.

This page crops the signature to 230 x 75 pixels where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 20 KB. A signature that small is usually under 10 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum with an invisible comment inside the file. The signature is exactly the same.
tips: Draw the box with a thin pen and sign inside it without touching the edges.
Photograph or scan it straight on in good light, then drag the crop box to the edges of the box you drew.
Save the result as Signature.jpg before you upload it.

faq.q: Can I change my TNPSC signature after uploading it?
faq.a: Yes, before you submit. TNPSC says to use the edit option in the online application to upload the signature again, and to save it before the final submission. Details carried over from your One Time Registration are changed with Edit profile in the OTR first.

faq.q: Where do I sign at the TNPSC exam?
faq.a: You sign in Part II on page 1 of the OMR answer sheet. Candidates with a benchmark disability also put a left thumb impression there if possible, and scribe users who cannot sign may give the thumb impression alone.

faq.q: What resolution should the TNPSC signature scan be?
faq.a: TNPSC asks you to scan the paper with the signed box at 200 DPI, then crop it to just the box. An unclear image, or one in the wrong size or format, can lead to the online application being rejected, so scan in good light with the pen strokes sharp.

pages.description: Compress the certificates for your TNPSC application to a PDF of 200 KB or less for each claim. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: TNPSC asks for the certificates behind each claim in your application as one PDF of no more than 200 KB. A scan of a page or two is often several megabytes, so it is compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting TNPSC certificates under 200 KB
paragraphs: TNPSC's Instructions to Applicants say the certificates supporting every claim in the online application are uploaded with it, as one PDF file of not more than 200 KB for each claim, with one page or several. That covers the certificates for age, education, community and any other claim you make.

We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits under 200 KB, so the text stays as readable as the limit allows. Real text in a PDF is never blurred, only scanned images.
tips: Put all the pages for one claim in one PDF, then compress that PDF here.
At the later on-screen certificate verification, TNPSC asks for PDFs of 300 KB to 500 KB scanned at 200 DPI. Pick that limit under Use a different limit when you get there.
If a certificate is a photo, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF).

faq.q: Can I re-upload a TNPSC certificate after submitting my application?
faq.a: Yes. You can check your uploaded certificates through your One Time Registration, and upload or re-upload them until two days before the hall tickets for that post are put online, which is twelve days before the exam. An application without the required documents, uploaded clearly and legibly by then, is rejected.

faq.q: Do I upload my certificates again for every TNPSC application?
faq.a: Not within two years. TNPSC links uploaded certificates to your One Time Registration and keeps them for up to two years, showing them for you to confirm when you apply for another post. After two years you upload all of them again.

faq.q: Can I upload my TNPSC certificates from an e-seva centre?
faq.a: Yes. TNPSC allows the certificates to be uploaded from any source, including e-seva centres. Whoever uploads them, each claim still goes in as one PDF of no more than 200 KB, so compress the PDF before you go if the scan is larger.

guide.title: Getting a UPPSC photo to 5 x 6 cm and under 50 KB
paragraphs: UPPSC's scanning guidelines ask for the photograph in true colour, 5 cm wide and 6 cm high, scanned at 200 DPI, with a file of no more than 50 KB. You upload it once in the One Time Registration, and it is used for UPPSC's exam applications.
At 200 DPI, 5 x 6 cm comes to 394 x 472 pixels. This page crops the photo to that size where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 50 KB.
tips: Use a recent passport-size photo on a light background, and crop close around your head and shoulders.
If you scan a printed photo, paste it on white paper and scan at 200 DPI, as the guidelines describe.
Each UPPSC advertisement can add its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What is the UPPSC photo size in KB and pixels?
faq.a: UPPSC asks for the photo 5 cm wide and 6 cm high at 200 DPI, under 50 KB. The guidelines give the size in centimetres, and at 200 DPI that is 394 x 472 pixels, which is what this page makes.

faq.q: Can I scan my UPPSC photo and signature on one sheet?
faq.a: Yes, that is the method UPPSC describes: paste the photo on white paper, sign in the signature space, scan the sheet, then crop the photo and the signature to their own sizes. Upload the same scan here for the photo and on the UPPSC signature page for the signature.

faq.q: Is there a minimum file size for the UPPSC photo?
faq.a: UPPSC's scanning guidelines give only a maximum: the photo must be no more than 50 KB. So this page does not pad the photo up to any minimum.

guide.title: Getting a UPPSC signature to 6 x 3 cm and under 30 KB
paragraphs: UPPSC's scanning guidelines ask for the signature 6 cm wide and 3 cm high, scanned at 200 DPI, with a file of no more than 30 KB. The signature must be in full and in your own hand: initials and signatures in capital letters are not accepted.
At 200 DPI, 6 x 3 cm comes to 472 x 236 pixels. This page crops the signature to that size where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 30 KB.
tips: Sign in full with a dark pen on plain white paper, the same way you will sign at the exam.
The signature goes on your admit card, and a signature in the answer sheet that does not match it can disqualify you.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.

faq.q: What is the UPPSC signature size in KB?
faq.a: The UPPSC signature must be no more than 30 KB, 6 cm wide and 3 cm high, scanned at 200 DPI. That is a wide shape, twice as wide as it is tall, so sign across the space instead of in a narrow block.

faq.q: Can someone else sign for me on the UPPSC form?
faq.a: No. UPPSC's guidelines say the signature must be signed only by the applicant. It is treated as proof of identity and must be genuine and in full, so nobody else can sign on your behalf.

faq.q: Should the UPPSC signature be in colour or black and white?
faq.a: UPPSC's table asks for true colour for the signature as well as the photo, so scan or photograph it in colour instead of saving it as a black and white image. This page keeps the colours of the image you upload.

pages.blurb: BPSC's registration takes a picture of your Hindi and English signatures under 20 KB, 150 to 220 pixels wide and 250 to 320 pixels high. This page makes it 200 x 300 pixels, inside both ranges.

source.label: BPSC's user manual for online registration

guide.title: Getting a BPSC signature under 20 KB
paragraphs: In the BPSC One Time Registration on bpsconline.bihar.gov.in, the photo step takes a live photo with your webcam, and you upload a picture of your Hindi and English signatures. BPSC's user manual says the picture should be less than 20 KB, with a width between 150 and 220 pixels and a height between 250 and 320 pixels. That is taller than it is wide.
This page crops the picture to 200 x 300 pixels where you place the crop box, which is inside both ranges, and saves it at the best quality under 20 KB.
tips: Signing one above the other on white paper fits the tall shape: the Hindi signature, then the English one below it.
If the form asks for each signature as its own picture, make each one on this page.
Your photo is not uploaded from a file: the registration captures it live, so sit in good light facing the webcam.

faq.q: Where do I upload the signature in the BPSC registration?
faq.a: It is Step 6, Photo and Signature, of the profile you create after registering, following your qualification and experience details. After it you save the profile, accept the terms and conditions, and click Submit and lock profile.

faq.q: How do I change my BPSC signature after locking the profile?
faq.a: Go to the My Account tab and choose Update/Unlock Profile. BPSC sends an OTP to your registered email and mobile number, and after you enter it you can edit the profile, including the signature. Lock the profile again when you finish.

faq.q: What does BPSC ask for in the live photo?
faq.a: Keep your face straight in front of the webcam with your eyes open, in good light against a light coloured background. Do not wear a cap, glasses, sunglasses, mask, muffler or helmet, and make sure no one else is in the frame. A live photo is captured again when you apply for a post.

guide.title: Getting a Kerala PSC photo to 150 x 200 and 30 KB
paragraphs: Kerala PSC's instructions ask for the photograph as a JPEG 200 pixels high and 150 pixels wide, of no more than 30 KB. Since the start of 2025, a new profile needs a photo taken within the last six months, with your name and the date it was taken printed clearly at the bottom. Once accepted, the photo stays valid for 10 years.
This page crops the photo to 150 x 200 pixels where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 30 KB.
tips: Get the name and date printed on the photo at the studio. This page does not add text.
Place the crop box so it keeps the name and date at the bottom, and your face clear above it.
The photo is uploaded once to your profile and used for every post you apply for.

faq.q: Can I wear a cap or goggles in my Kerala PSC photo?
faq.a: No. Kerala PSC asks for the uploaded photo to be taken without a cap or goggles, except headwear worn for religious custom. Your face and shoulders should be clear, against a white or light background, with your face centred and your eyes open.

faq.q: What is the Kerala PSC profile photo size in pixels and KB?
faq.a: The photo is uploaded as a JPG 200 pixels high and 150 pixels wide, of no more than 30 KB, with your name and the date it was taken printed at the bottom. A Kerala PSC notification states that applications with photos not meeting these rules are rejected and cannot be appealed.

faq.q: Do I need a printed photo at the Kerala PSC exam centre?
faq.a: Yes. You fix a passport-size photo, taken within the past six months, on the Identification Certificate. It should be 4.5 x 3.5 cm, colour or black and white, with a white or light background. Candidates who come without it, or with a photo of the wrong size, are not allowed to write the exam.

guide.title: Getting a Kerala PSC signature to 150 x 100 and 30 KB
paragraphs: Kerala PSC's One Time Registration instructions ask for the signature image at 150 x 100 pixels and no more than 30 KB, as a JPEG. It goes into your profile with the photo, and is used for every post you apply for.
This page crops the signature to 150 x 100 pixels where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 30 KB.
tips: Sign with a dark pen on plain white paper, and photograph or scan it in good light.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What size should the Kerala PSC signature be?
faq.a: Kerala PSC asks for the scanned signature at 150 x 100 pixels, clearly legible, and no larger than 30 KB, as a JPEG. The same signature stays in your One Time Registration profile and is used for the posts you apply for.

faq.q: Where do I sign at the Kerala PSC exam?
faq.a: At the exam, you sign across the photo on your Identification Certificate in front of the Assistant Superintendent, so part of the signature is on the photo and part on the paper. You also sign beneath the declaration on it and against your name in the hall's address list.
