guide.title: Getting an APPSC photo under 50 KB
paragraphs: APPSC's One Time Profile Registration form asks for the photograph as a JPG or JPEG, 3.5 cm wide and 4.5 cm high, and refuses a file of 50 KB or more. It can be in colour or black and white, taken without a cap or goggles (glasses are fine), and your name and the date it was taken must be printed on the photo itself. Polaroid photos are not accepted.
The form sets no pixel size, so this page keeps the photo as large as fits under 50 KB. It reduces the size step by step and stops at the first step that fits.
tips: Get the name and date printed on the photo at the studio. This page does not add text.
Crop the photo to passport shape, close around your head and shoulders, with the name and date strip kept in.
The form takes JPG or JPEG files only.

faq.q: What is the APPSC photo size in KB and cm?
faq.a: APPSC's One Time Profile Registration form takes the photograph as a JPG or JPEG under 50 KB, sized 3.5 cm wide by 4.5 cm high. The form shows a sample photograph next to these rules so you can compare yours before uploading.

faq.q: Do I need my photo scanned before starting the APPSC OTPR?
faq.a: Yes. APPSC asks you to have the scanned photograph and signature ready before you begin, along with your educational certificates for reference. What you enter in the OTPR form is treated as final and used as it is, so check the photo before you submit.

faq.q: Where is the photo uploaded in the APPSC OTPR form?
faq.a: The photo is uploaded in the Photo & Signature Details section, which comes after the education and qualification details. The upload box under Photograph of the Candidate takes JPG or JPEG files only. After it come the notification alerts choice and the declaration.

pages.title: APPSC signature

guide.title: Getting an APPSC signature under 30 KB
paragraphs: APPSC's One Time Profile Registration form asks for the signature as a JPG or JPEG, 3.5 cm wide and 1.5 cm high, and refuses a file of 30 KB or more.
The form sets no pixel size, so this page keeps the signature as large as fits under 30 KB. It reduces the size step by step and stops at the first step that fits.
tips: Sign with a dark pen on plain white paper, and crop close around the signature so it has the long, low shape of 3.5 x 1.5 cm.
Photograph or scan it straight on, in good light without shadows.
The form takes JPG or JPEG files only.

faq.q: What is the APPSC signature size in KB?
faq.a: The APPSC registration form takes the signature as a JPG or JPEG under 30 KB, sized 3.5 cm wide by 1.5 cm high. A sample signature is shown beside the rule, which helps you judge the long, low shape before you upload.

faq.q: Should I scan the whole page for my APPSC signature?
faq.a: No. APPSC's portal FAQ says to scan only the area holding the photograph or signature, and not the complete page. Crop close around your signature so it fills the image, which also keeps the file small.

faq.q: Do I have to confirm my APPSC OTPR after uploading the signature?
faq.a: No further confirmation is needed. The OTPR form says a registration that goes through successfully is treated as confirmed. Note down the OTPR Reference ID it gives you, since APPSC asks you to use it for future correspondence.

pages.blurb: TGPSC's 2026 notifications ask for a recent colour passport-size photo between 100 KB and 200 KB, as a JPG or PNG. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting a TGPSC photo to 100 KB to 200 KB
paragraphs: TGPSC's 2026 recruitment notifications ask for a recent colour passport-size photograph, taken no more than 3 months before the last date of the application, as a JPG or PNG file between 100 KB and 200 KB. That minimum is high: a small, cropped photo can be under it.
This page keeps the photo as large as fits under 200 KB. If a JPEG comes out under 100 KB, it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file, so the photo is exactly the same.
tips: Upload a JPG: only a JPEG can be padded up to the 100 KB minimum. A PNG keeps its format.
Crop the photo close around your head and shoulders, against a plain light background.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What is the TGPSC photo size in KB?
faq.a: TGPSC's 2026 notification asks for a recent colour passport-size photograph between 100 KB and 200 KB, in JPG or PNG format. It must be taken no more than 3 months before the last date of the application.

faq.q: What if my photo on the TGPSC hall ticket is blurred?
faq.a: If the hall ticket photo is too small, blurred or defective, fix a passport-size photo in the space at the bottom of the hall ticket, get it attested by a Gazetted Officer, and give an undertaking. Hand a similar photo to the Chief Superintendent for the Nominal Roll.

faq.q: Do I need a TGPSC ID before applying with my photo?
faq.a: Yes. If you have not registered before, fill the OTR form on tgpsc.gov.in to get a TGPSC ID. You then open the Online Application link, enter the TGPSC ID and date of birth, and log in with the OTP sent to your registered mobile number.

pages.blurb: TGPSC's 2026 notifications ask for the scanned signature between 20 KB and 30 KB, as a JPG or PNG. A clean signature is often under 20 KB, so a JPEG is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a TGPSC signature to 20 KB to 30 KB
paragraphs: TGPSC's 2026 recruitment notifications ask for a scanned specimen signature as a JPG or PNG file between 20 KB and 30 KB. The range is narrow, so a signature has to land between the two.
This page keeps the signature as large as fits under 30 KB. If a JPEG comes out under 20 KB, it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file, so the signature is exactly the same.
tips: Upload a JPG: only a JPEG can be padded up to the 20 KB minimum. A PNG keeps its format.
Sign with a dark pen on plain white paper and crop close around the signature.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What is the TGPSC signature size in KB?
faq.a: TGPSC asks for a scanned specimen signature of 20 KB to 30 KB, in JPG or PNG format. Both limits apply, so a very clean, small signature file can fall below the minimum as easily as a large scan goes over the maximum.

faq.q: How is my signature used at the TGPSC exam?
faq.a: The invigilator checks your identity against the signature and photograph on the Nominal Roll and your Hall Ticket. You also sign the OMR Answer Sheet, have the invigilator sign it, and sign the Nominal Roll in the place given.

faq.q: Can TGPSC fix a wrong signature after I submit?
faq.a: The notification says the Commission will not make any changes to a submitted application form. Check the preview, including the uploaded signature, before you click CONFIRM & SUBMIT, since the particulars are saved only after that button.

pages.description: Resize your photo to 110 x 140 pixels and 40 KB or less for an HPPSC (Himachal Pradesh) online application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: HPPSC asks for the scanned photograph at 110 pixels wide by 140 high, no more than 40 KB, as a .jpg.

guide.title: Getting an HPPSC photo to 110 x 140 and 40 KB
paragraphs: HPPSC's answers for online applicants say the scanned photograph should be 140 pixels high and 110 pixels wide, as a .jpg of no more than 40 KB. Colour and black and white are both accepted, as long as the photo is clear. You register once, and the profile is used for every post you apply for.
This page crops the photo to 110 x 140 pixels where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 40 KB.
tips: Crop close around your head and shoulders, so your face is clear at this small size.
Use a recent passport-size photo against a plain light background.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: Where do I upload my photo on the HPPSC portal?
faq.a: HPPSC's online application has a Photo & Signature Upload module, where the photograph and signature are uploaded as .jpg files. The photo should be 110 pixels wide by 140 pixels high and no more than 40 KB.

faq.q: My photo is a .bmp or .tiff file. Will HPPSC accept it?
faq.a: HPPSC asks for a .jpg. Its FAQ says to open a photo in another format, such as .tiff or .bmp, in MS Paint or IrfanView and use Save As to save it as .jpg. Then bring the .jpg here to crop and compress it.

faq.q: How do I get my HPPSC photo to the right pixel size?
faq.a: HPPSC's FAQ suggests cropping away the unneeded area and then resizing to the stated pixel size in an image editor. This page does both in one go: it crops to 110 x 140 pixels where you place the crop box, then saves under 40 KB.

pages.description: Resize your signature to 140 x 110 pixels and 40 KB or less for an HPPSC (Himachal Pradesh) online application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: HPPSC asks for the scanned signature at 140 pixels wide by 110 high, no more than 40 KB, signed in black ink on white paper.

guide.title: Getting an HPPSC signature to 140 x 110 and 40 KB
paragraphs: HPPSC's answers for online applicants say to sign on white paper with a black ink pen and scan it, with the image 110 pixels high and 140 pixels wide, as a .jpg of no more than 40 KB.
This page crops the signature to 140 x 110 pixels where you place the crop box and saves it at the best quality under 40 KB.
tips: Sign with a black pen on plain white paper, a little smaller than usual so it fits the near-square shape.
Take the photo close around the signature, then drag the crop box so it keeps all of it.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What pixel size is the HPPSC signature?
faq.a: The HPPSC signature is 140 pixels wide by 110 pixels high, no more than 40 KB, as a .jpg. That is the photo's size turned on its side (the photo is 110 wide by 140 high), so check you have the signature page open and not the photo one.

faq.q: Do I register again with HPPSC to apply for another post?
faq.a: No. If you have registered with HPPSC for any exam, you do not need to register again. Your saved profile, with the user ID and password, is used for later notifications, and you apply with the Click to Apply button against each post.

faq.q: Can I change my HPPSC signature after submitting the application?
faq.a: HPPSC's FAQ says applications are final once submitted, and no changes can be made after that. Check that the uploaded signature is clear and complete before you submit.

pages.heading: APSC photo: 50 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: APSC photo
pages.description: Compress your photo to between 50 KB and 200 KB for the APSC (Assam) One Time Registration. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: APSC's One Time Registration takes the photo between 50 KB and 200 KB, taken no more than 3 months ago. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting an APSC photo to 50 KB to 200 KB
paragraphs: APSC's advertisements say the One Time Registration on apscrecruitment.in takes a photo of at least 50 KB and at most 200 KB, not older than 3 months, along with your signature and other details. You then apply for each post from the same registration.

APSC sets no pixel size, so this page keeps the photo as large as fits under 200 KB. If a JPEG comes out under 50 KB, it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file, so the photo is exactly the same.
tips: Upload a JPG photo: only a JPEG can be padded up to the 50 KB minimum.
Crop close around your head and shoulders, against a plain light background.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What is the APSC photo size in KB?
faq.a: APSC's One Time Registration takes the photo with a minimum size of 50 KB and a maximum of 200 KB. The photo must not be older than 3 months. The signature has the same 50 KB to 200 KB range.

faq.q: Where do I upload my photo for APSC?
faq.a: Go to apscrecruitment.in and click Register Here to create an account, then log in. The photo is uploaded in the One Time Registration details, together with your personal information, educational qualification, work experience and signature.

faq.q: Can I change my APSC photo after final submission?
faq.a: No. APSC does not allow editing after final submission, so check every field first. After the preview you can click Submit for final submission, or Cancel to go back and make corrections.

pages.heading: APSC signature: 50 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: APSC signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to between 50 KB and 200 KB for the APSC (Assam) One Time Registration. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: APSC's One Time Registration takes the signature between 50 KB and 200 KB. A signature is usually far under 50 KB, so a JPEG is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting an APSC signature to 50 KB to 200 KB
paragraphs: APSC's advertisements give the same range for the signature as for the photo in the One Time Registration: at least 50 KB and at most 200 KB. For a signature, the minimum is the hard part, since a clean signature image is often 10 KB to 30 KB.
This page keeps the signature as large as fits under 200 KB. If a JPEG comes out under 50 KB, it is padded up to it with an invisible comment inside the file, so the signature is exactly the same.
tips: Upload a JPG: only a JPEG can be padded up to the 50 KB minimum. A PNG keeps its format.
Sign with a dark pen on plain white paper and crop close around the signature.
Each notification can set its own rules. If yours states a different size, change it under Change size or pixels before you compress.

faq.q: What is the APSC signature size in KB?
faq.a: APSC asks for the signature with a minimum of 50 KB and a maximum of 200 KB, the same range as the photo. A scanned signature is often well under 50 KB, so the minimum is the limit most people need to reach.

faq.q: What size do APSC certificate uploads need to be?
faq.a: Certificates and documents supporting your claims, such as date of birth, experience and qualifications, are uploaded as PDFs of no more than 2 MB that stay legible when printed. APSC suggests scanning them at 200 dpi in grey scale.

faq.q: What happens after I submit my APSC signature in the OTR?
faq.a: Once your One Time Registration details are submitted, you can download them. To apply for a post, open Applicant Section, then Apply Section. The same registration, with its signature, is used for each post you apply for.

pages.blurb: The NEET (UG) form asks for a passport-size photograph as a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. A phone photo is usually several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting a NEET photo under 200 KB
paragraphs: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a recent passport-size photograph, in colour or black and white, as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. 80% of the image should be your face, without a mask, with the ears visible, against a white background.
The bulletin sets no pixel size, so this page keeps the photo as large as fits under 200 KB, which leaves it sharp. It reduces the size step by step and stops at the first step that fits.
tips: Crop the photo close around your head and shoulders before you upload it, so your face fills most of the frame.
Use the same photo you will paste on the attendance sheet at the exam centre; the bulletin asks for the same one.
The form also takes a live photo with your webcam or phone. That one is not uploaded from a file.

faq.q: How recent does my NEET photo need to be?
faq.a: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a passport-size photograph taken on or after 1 January 2026. Upload only your own latest photo: NTA gives no chance to correct it later, and a photo of someone else is treated as unfair means.

faq.q: Can I upload a Polaroid or computer-made photo for NEET?
faq.a: No. The bulletin says Polaroid and computer-generated photos are not acceptable, and a photo that looks de-shaped, hand-made or computer made gets the application rejected. Spectacles are allowed only if you wear them regularly. This page only resizes and compresses the photo you give it and does not change the background.

faq.q: How many printed copies of my NEET photo should I keep?
faq.a: The bulletin advises keeping 6 to 8 passport-size and 4 to 6 postcard-size (4 x 6 inch) colour prints with a white background, as the same photo is used for the exam, counselling and admission. On exam day you also bring one postcard-size colour photo with a white background.

pages.heading: NEET UG signature: JPEG, 10 KB to 100 KB
pages.title: NEET (UG) signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB for the NEET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The NEET (UG) form asks for your signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB. A phone photo of it is far bigger, and a tightly cropped one can come out under 10 KB, so it is padded up to the minimum if needed.

guide.title: Getting a NEET signature to 10 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the signature file as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB, clearly legible. It sets no pixel size.
The image is kept as large as fits under 100 KB. If it comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum with an invisible comment inside the file, so the signature itself is unchanged.
tips: Sign on plain white paper in dark ink and photograph it in good light, without shadows.
Crop close around the signature first, so it is not a small mark in a large white page.
There is no correction window for the signature, so check it is legible before you upload it.

faq.q: Does my scribe need to upload a signature for NEET?
faq.a: Yes, if you use a scribe. The NEET (UG) 2026 bulletin asks for the scribe's scanned signature in the same 10 KB to 100 KB range as yours, clearly legible. You can compress the scribe's signature on this page the same way as your own.

faq.q: Do I have to sign anything at the NEET exam centre?
faq.a: Yes. The bulletin says you sign the Attendance Sheet twice: once right after the exam starts and again when you hand your Answer Sheet to the invigilator. You also put your thumb impression there, so sign the way you did on the uploaded file.

faq.q: What else does NEET ask me to upload with the signature?
faq.a: In the same step you upload your photograph, your left and right hand fingers and thumb impressions as JPG or JPEG images, and your documents as PDFs. The bulletin says unclear finger and thumb impressions are rejected, so photograph them as carefully as the signature.

pages.heading: NEET UG certificates: PDF, 50 KB to 300 KB
pages.title: NEET (UG) certificates and documents
pages.description: Compress your Class 10 certificate, category certificate or address proof to a PDF under 300 KB for the NEET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The NEET (UG) form takes the Class 10 certificate, marksheet, category certificate, address proof and other documents as PDFs between 50 KB and 300 KB each. A scan is usually bigger.

guide.title: Getting a NEET document PDF under 300 KB
paragraphs: The NEET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the Class 10 certificate and marksheet, the category certificate, the PwD or UDID certificate and the present and permanent address proofs as PDFs between 50 KB and 300 KB, clearly legible.

A one-page scan fits in 300 KB comfortably. We lower the resolution of the scan step by step and keep the first step that fits, so the text stays as sharp as the limit allows. A real scan is rarely under 50 KB; if yours is, scan it at a higher resolution.
tips: Make one PDF per document, as the form asks for each one separately.
If your document is a photo, save it as a PDF first (most phones can print to PDF), then compress it here.
Scan flat and in good light, with the whole page in the frame, so it stays legible at a small size.

faq.q: What do I upload for NEET if my Class 10 marks are in CGPA?
faq.a: The NEET (UG) 2026 bulletin asks for a conversion or equivalence certificate as well, as a separate PDF between 50 KB and 300 KB. Your Class 10 certificate or the equivalency certificate should also show your date of birth.

faq.q: Which document does an NRI or OCI candidate upload for NEET?
faq.a: Candidates whose nationality is not Indian upload their NRI, OCI or foreigner certificate or other documentary proof as a PDF between 50 KB and 300 KB. It goes in alongside the Class 10 documents and address proofs, each as its own file.

faq.q: What extra PDFs does a PwD candidate upload for NEET?
faq.a: Besides the PwD, PwBD or UDID certificate, the bulletin lists a certificate of physical limitation to write, an undertaking for using your own scribe, and the scribe's qualification certificate where they apply. Each is a clearly legible file between 50 KB and 300 KB.

pages.heading: JEE Main photo: JPEG, 10 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: JEE (Main) photo
pages.description: Compress your passport-size photo to a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB for the JEE (Main) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The JEE (Main) form asks for a colour passport-size photograph as a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed to fit.

guide.title: Getting a JEE Main photo under 200 KB
paragraphs: The JEE (Main) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a recent passport-size photograph in colour, with 80% of the face visible including the ears, without a mask, against a white background, as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB.
No pixel size is set, so the photo is kept as large as fits under 200 KB. Each step down is a little smaller, and the first one that fits is the one you get.
tips: Crop close around your head and shoulders first; the bulletin wants the face to fill most of the photo.
Keep your details on Aadhaar up to date. NTA matches your photos against them.
You also take a live photo during the application. That one comes from your webcam or phone, not from a file.

faq.q: Can I upload a black and white photo for JEE Main?
faq.a: No. The JEE (Main) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the passport-size photograph in colour, between 10 KB and 200 KB. The NEET (UG) bulletin allows black and white, so a photo you made for NEET may not suit JEE Main.

faq.q: What background does the JEE Main live photo need?
faq.a: For the live photo taken with your webcam or phone while filling the form, the bulletin asks for a light-coloured background, proper lighting and 80% of your face visible, including ears and without a mask. If your computer has no webcam, scan the QR code on the form with a phone.

faq.q: What if I do not verify my identity with Aadhaar for JEE Main?
faq.a: Then you also upload a scanned identity proof as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB, clearly legible. That is the same range as the photo, so you can compress the identity proof on this page as well.

pages.heading: JEE Main signature: JPEG, 10 KB to 100 KB
pages.title: JEE (Main) signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB for the JEE (Main) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The JEE (Main) form asks for the signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB. If a cropped signature comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a JEE Main signature to 10 KB to 100 KB
paragraphs: The JEE (Main) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the signature file as a clearly legible JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB, with no pixel size given.

It is saved at the highest quality that fits under 100 KB. A small, clean signature can come out under 10 KB, and then it is padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file. Nothing in the picture changes.
tips: Use a dark pen on white paper so the signature stays legible after compression.
Photograph it straight on, not at an angle, and crop away the rest of the page.
The same bulletin asks for the Class 10 certificate as a PDF of 50 KB to 300 KB. The NEET certificates page uses the same limits.

faq.q: What is the JEE Main signature size in KB?
faq.a: The JEE (Main) 2026 bulletin asks for the signature as a clearly legible JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 100 KB. That is half the 200 KB allowed for the photo, so a signature saved with photo settings may be too big.

faq.q: Can I change my JEE Main signature after submitting the form?
faq.a: The bulletin says to upload your own signature correctly because the facility for correction will not be given later. Uploading someone else's signature, or a wrong or morphed one, is treated as unfair means.

faq.q: Is my JEE Main signature checked at the exam centre?
faq.a: Yes. During entry, along with frisking and biometric registration, the invigilator cross-checks your admit card and matches your signature and photo. Sign on paper the same way you signed the uploaded image.

pages.heading: GATE 2027 photo: 3.5 x 4.5 cm JPEG under 600 KB
pages.title: GATE 2027 photo
pages.description: Crop your photo to passport size, 350 x 450 pixels, as a JPEG under 600 KB for the GATE 2027 application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: GATE 2027 takes a passport-size colour photo between 200 x 260 and 530 x 690 pixels, up to 600 KB. A phone photo is far bigger and the wrong shape, so it is cropped to 350 x 450 and saved as a JPEG.

guide.title: Getting a GATE photo to the right shape and size
paragraphs: The GATE 2027 Information Brochure asks for a colour passport-size photograph, 3.5 cm wide and 4.5 cm high, as a JPEG. Its width-to-height ratio must be between 0.66 and 0.89, it must be between 200 x 260 and 530 x 690 pixels, and the file can be up to 600 KB.

This page crops the photo to 350 x 450 pixels, the 3.5 to 4.5 shape and well inside both pixel limits, where you place the crop box. At that size a photo is far under 600 KB, so it is saved at high quality.
tips: Place the crop box so your face fills most of the frame: the brochure asks for the face to cover 60 to 70% of the image after cropping.
Use a plain white background, look straight at the camera, and avoid glare on glasses.
This photo appears on your admit card and score card, and a live photo is also taken during registration.

faq.q: How old can my GATE 2027 photo be?
faq.a: The GATE 2027 Information Brochure asks for a latest photo that is not older than 3 months. A live photo is also captured during registration, so use a computer with a webcam or a phone with a 5 MP camera.

faq.q: Can I wear glasses or a head covering in my GATE photo?
faq.a: Normal spectacles are allowed, but not with glare; if the glare cannot be avoided, take them off. Caps, hats, sunglasses and coloured glasses are not allowed. A head covering is accepted only for religious reasons, with your face visible from chin to forehead and edge to edge.

faq.q: What happens if GATE rejects my photo?
faq.a: A photo that does not meet the brochure's rules can lead to rejection of the application, and the fee is not refunded. Applications are checked for photo clarity, and defects are sent to you by email, SMS or WhatsApp to fix within a set time, so check your status on the portal.

pages.heading: GATE 2027 signature: up to 580 x 180 pixels, under 300 KB
pages.title: GATE 2027 signature
pages.description: Crop your signature to 480 x 160 pixels, a JPEG under 300 KB, for the GATE 2027 application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: GATE 2027 takes a signature JPEG between 250 x 80 and 580 x 180 pixels, with a height to width ratio from 1:2.75 to 1:3.75, up to 300 KB. A photo of a signature is cropped to 480 x 160 to fit all three.

guide.title: Getting a GATE signature to the right shape
paragraphs: The GATE 2027 Information Brochure asks for the signature as a JPEG with a height to width ratio of 1 to between 2.75 and 3.75, between 250 x 80 and 580 x 180 pixels, and up to 300 KB. After cropping, the signature should cover 70 to 80% of the image.
This page crops it to 480 x 160 pixels, a ratio of 1 to 3, inside both pixel limits, where you place the crop box. A signature at that size is a small file, so it is saved at high quality.
tips: Sign in black or dark blue ink on white paper; the brochure accepts no other colours.
Drag the crop box tight around the signature so it fills most of the image.
Sign the way you will at the exam: a signature that does not match can lead to disqualification.

faq.q: Why does GATE reject my signature?
faq.a: The brochure shows signatures it does not accept: on a dark background, in all capital letters, digital signatures, initials only, ink other than blue or black, too small to read, with a background or other writing, or not signed horizontally. Sign your full signature on plain white paper.

faq.q: Where does my GATE signature appear after I apply?
faq.a: It is printed on your admit card. The brochure says the admit card is valid only if your photograph and signature on it are clear, and you bring a printout of it on A4 paper, preferably in colour, to the exam with your original photo ID.

faq.q: What pixel size is the GATE 2027 signature?
faq.a: The brochure allows 250 x 80 up to 580 x 180 pixels, with a height to width ratio from 1:2.75 to 1:3.75, and a file of up to 300 KB. This page crops to 480 x 160 pixels, which meets all three. Only you may sign it.

pages.heading: CUET UG photo: JPEG, 10 KB to 200 KB
pages.title: CUET (UG) photo
pages.description: Compress your passport-size photo to a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB for the CUET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The CUET (UG) form asks for a recent colour passport-size photo as a JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. A phone photo is several megabytes, so it is resized and compressed until it fits.

guide.title: Getting a CUET photo under 200 KB
paragraphs: The CUET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for a scanned passport-size photograph in colour, with 80% of the face visible including the ears, without a mask, against a white background, as a JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB.
The bulletin gives no pixel size, so the photo stays as large as 200 KB allows. Each attempt is a little smaller than the last, and you get the first one that fits.
tips: Crop around your head and shoulders before uploading, so your face fills most of the photo.
Besides this upload, the form takes a live photo with your webcam or phone.
NTA checks photos against your Aadhaar details, so keep your Aadhaar photo recent.

faq.q: What is the CUET photo size in KB?
faq.a: The CUET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the photograph as a clearly legible JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 200 KB. This page compresses it under 200 KB, and if a JPEG comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum without changing the picture.

faq.q: Do I need a printed photo for the CUET exam?
faq.a: Yes. Bring an extra photograph, the same one you uploaded, to paste on the attendance sheet in the exam room. You also carry the printed admit card with the filled-in self declaration and an original photo ID such as Aadhaar, PAN card or passport.

faq.q: Can NTA fix my CUET photo after I submit the form?
faq.a: The bulletin lists your photograph among the details you must make sure are correct and your own, and says NTA does not edit or alter any information after the application process is complete. Check the uploaded photo before you submit.

pages.heading: CUET UG signature: JPEG, 10 KB to 50 KB
pages.title: CUET (UG) signature
pages.description: Compress your signature to a JPEG between 10 KB and 50 KB for the CUET (UG) application. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: The CUET (UG) form takes the signature as a JPEG between 10 KB and 50 KB, half the limit NEET and JEE Main allow. If it comes out under 10 KB, it is padded up to the minimum without changing it.

guide.title: Getting a CUET signature to 10 KB to 50 KB
paragraphs: The CUET (UG) 2026 Information Bulletin asks for the signature file as a clearly legible JPG or JPEG between 10 KB and 50 KB. It gives no pixel size.

The signature is kept as large as fits under 50 KB. A small, clean one can come out under 10 KB, and then it is padded up to 10 KB with an invisible comment inside the file, so the image is unchanged.
tips: The CUET limit is 50 KB, lower than NEET and JEE Main, so a signature made for those may need compressing again.
Sign in dark ink on plain white paper and photograph it straight on, in good light.
Crop away the rest of the page so the signature fills the image.

faq.q: What if the signature on my CUET admit card looks wrong?
faq.a: If your photograph or signature on the admit card or confirmation page does not match your details, contact the NTA help line between 10 AM and 5 PM. You still appear in the exam with the admit card you downloaded, and NTA corrects the record later.

faq.q: What else goes in the same CUET upload step as the signature?
faq.a: The CUET (UG) form uploads the photograph (JPG or JPEG, 10 KB to 200 KB), the signature and, if it applies, the disability or UDID certificate as a PDF between 50 KB and 300 KB. Each file has its own size range, so compress them separately.

faq.q: Can I upload a signature someone else made for CUET?
faq.a: No. The bulletin says to upload your own photograph, signature and certificates. Using someone else's signature, or uploading a wrong or morphed one, is treated as unfair means, so sign it yourself on plain paper.

pages.heading: IRCC document upload: PDF under 4 MB for Canadian immigration
pages.title: IRCC document upload
pages.description: Compress a scanned document to a PDF under 4 MB for IRCC: the secure account, Permanent Residence Portal, citizenship and asylum uploads. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Most IRCC accounts take files up to 4 MB, and the IRCC Portal up to 5 MB. A PDF under 4 MB uploads to any of them. Multi-page scans are usually far bigger.

source.label: the IRCC Help Centre's file size limits

guide.title: Getting an IRCC document under 4 MB
paragraphs: IRCC sets the limit per account: 4 MB for the IRCC secure account, the Permanent Residence Portal, the online citizenship application and the asylum portal, and 5 MB for the IRCC Portal. Aiming under 4 MB means the same file works wherever you upload it.

Each upload field takes one file, so a document with several pages, such as a passport or a set of bank statements, has to be a single PDF. Scanned at full quality that is often 10 to 30 MB. Here the scan's resolution is lowered step by step and the first step that fits is kept, so text stays as sharp as 4 MB allows.
tips: Combine all the pages into one PDF first. If you upload several files to one field, IRCC keeps only the last one.
Scanning at 150 to 300 DPI is plenty; higher only makes a bigger file to shrink.
Some IRCC forms set a lower limit, as low as 2 MB. If the upload page states one, choose that size instead.
This page is for documents. IRCC photos must be the photographer's original file, not altered in any way, so upload those as they are.

faq.q: Is the IRCC 4 MB limit per file or for the whole application?
faq.a: Per file. IRCC lists its limits as a size per file for each account type, 4 MB for most and 5 MB for the IRCC Portal. A 30-page PDF and a one-page PDF have the same limit, so a long multi-page document is the one most likely to need compressing.

faq.q: My Word document is too big for IRCC. What should I do?
faq.a: IRCC suggests removing unnecessary images, then saving as a PDF with the Minimum size option under Optimize for in Word. If that PDF is still over the limit, compress it here to bring it under 4 MB.

faq.q: Will compressing my IRCC PDF make the text hard to read?
faq.a: Text typed into the PDF is kept as text and stays sharp. Scanned pages are images, and their resolution is lowered step by step until the file fits. IRCC itself suggests saving images at 96 or 150 DPI to cut file size, so a lower resolution for scans is what it expects.

pages.heading: Discord emoji GIF: 128 x 128 under 256 KB
pages.title: Discord custom emoji
pages.description: Crop a GIF to 128 x 128 and fit it under 256 KB for a Discord custom emoji, still animated. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Discord takes custom emoji under 256 KB, at up to 128 x 128 pixels. A GIF from a phone or a GIF site is usually far bigger, so it is cropped to 128 x 128 and compressed until it fits, still animated.

source.label: Discord's help article on adding emojis

guide.title: Getting a GIF under Discord's emoji limit
paragraphs: Discord's help center says a custom emoji file must be smaller than 256 KB, and that emoji look best uploaded at up to 128 x 128 pixels, since they are shown at 32 x 32. Animated emoji are GIFs.

This page crops the GIF to 128 x 128 where you place the crop box, then compresses it to the largest file under 256 KB. Every frame keeps its timing, and the GIF still loops. If it cannot fit with every frame, some frames are dropped and the rest are held longer, so it plays at the same speed; the result says when that happened.
tips: Animated emoji use 50 extra slots that a server gets with Nitro or Nitro Basic.
Short loops fit best. A few seconds at 128 x 128 usually fits with every frame kept.
Choose Add a see-through border instead of cropping to keep the whole picture.

faq.q: Who can upload a custom emoji to a Discord server?
faq.a: The server owner, or anyone whose role has the Create Expressions permission. To edit or remove emoji, a role also needs Manage Expressions. An admin sets both in Server Settings, under Roles, then Permissions. Without that permission, a GIF of any size is refused.

faq.q: What can I name a Discord emoji?
faq.a: Emoji names must be at least 2 characters long and can use only letters, numbers and underscores, so a name like party_cat works and party-cat does not. You set the name when you upload the emoji in Server Settings, under the Emoji tab, or in Emoji Studio.

faq.q: Can I use a PNG or WEBP for a Discord emoji instead of a GIF?
faq.a: Yes. Discord takes custom emoji as JPEG, PNG, GIF or WEBP, each smaller than 256 KB. A PNG you drop here is cropped to 128 x 128 and stays a PNG. Animated emoji are GIFs, and they use the extra slots that come with Nitro or Nitro Basic.

source.label: Discord's help article on custom profiles

guide.title: Getting a GIF under Discord's banner limit
paragraphs: Discord's help center says banners must be PNG, JPG or animated GIF files under 10 MB, at least 680 x 240 pixels. Only Nitro members can upload an image or GIF as their profile banner.

This page crops the GIF to 680 x 240 where you place the crop box, so Discord does not have to crop it again, then compresses it to the largest file under 10 MB. Every frame keeps its timing, and the GIF still loops. If it cannot fit with every frame, some frames are dropped and the rest are held longer, so it plays at the same speed; the result says when that happened.
tips: Place the crop box over the part that matters: a wide clip cut from a tall video loses its top and bottom.
Long clips are the hardest to fit. Trim the GIF to the loop you want before uploading.
A still banner works the same way: drop a PNG or JPG instead.

faq.q: Where do I change my profile banner on Discord?
faq.a: On desktop, open User Settings with the cogwheel at the bottom left, go to the Profiles tab and select Change Banner. On mobile, tap your avatar at the bottom right, then Edit Profile. Upload the GIF made here, then save your changes.

faq.q: What happens if I press Skip on the Discord banner crop screen?
faq.a: After you upload a banner, Discord shows a crop step. Apply keeps the framing you set, and Skip crops the image with the default settings. A GIF cropped here to 680 x 240 already has the banner's shape and minimum size, so you set the framing here before you upload.

faq.q: Can my Discord avatar be an animated GIF as well as my banner?
faq.a: Yes, with Nitro. Nitro subscribers can upload animated GIFs as their avatar, and the avatar accepts PNG and GIF files. The avatar is a different shape from the 680 x 240 banner, so this page's crop is for the banner only.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under Discord's upload limit
paragraphs: Discord's File Attachments FAQ says that as of August 2026 the upload limit without Nitro is 20 MB, up from 10 MB. Nitro Basic raises it to 50 MB, and Nitro to up to 1 GB.

This page compresses the GIF to the largest file under 20 MB. It first tries fewer colours and gentle lossy compression; for bigger cuts it scales the frames down and, as a last step, drops some frames and holds the rest longer, so it plays at the same speed. Frame timing and looping are kept, and the result says if frames were dropped.
tips: Discord checks the size before it compresses anything, so the file you upload is the size that counts.
With Nitro Basic, open Change size or pixels and pick 50 MB instead.
To make the GIF smaller in pixels too, open Change size or pixels, then Exact size in pixels, and enter a width and height.

faq.q: Why does Discord on Android say my GIF is too big?
faq.a: Discord now checks the file size before compressing it, on mobile as well as desktop. Discord says Android users may hit the limit more often than before, because files there tend to be larger. Compress the GIF to under 20 MB here first, then upload it from your phone.

faq.q: Why does my GIF show as a download link in Discord?
faq.a: Discord's chat settings say that any image larger than 20 MB uploaded directly to Discord is shared as a download instead of being shown. Bringing the GIF under 20 MB here avoids that, and the GIF stays animated at its own pixel size.

faq.q: Can I send several GIFs in one Discord message?
faq.a: Yes. If you attach several images or GIFs to one message, Discord sends them together and shows them as a mosaic. Compress each large GIF here one at a time, then attach them all with the plus sign in the text field and send.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 500 KB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 500 KB for forum posts, profile pictures and chat. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: A short reaction GIF saved from a video is often several MB. To reach 500 KB it is compressed and usually made smaller in pixels, and it stays a GIF that plays at its own speed.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 500 KB
paragraphs: 500 KB is a tight limit for a GIF, because a GIF stores every frame as its own picture. A two-second loop at a few hundred pixels wide can fit; a long clip at full size cannot.

After a lossless cleanup we try lossy compression at full size, then fewer colours together with fewer pixels. Only if that is still too big are frames dropped, and the frames that stay are held longer, so it plays at the same speed. The result says if frames were dropped.
tips: Trim the GIF to the part that loops before you upload it. Fewer frames is the biggest saving there is.
Small GIFs with flat colours, like stickers and pixel art, fit far more easily than clips cut from video.
If the result is too small in pixels for you, a shorter clip will fit at a larger size.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 1 MB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 1 MB for chat apps, forums and email. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Many places that take GIFs cap them around 1 MB. A GIF over that is compressed to the largest file under 1 MB, and it keeps its frame timing and loop.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 1 MB
paragraphs: At 1 MB a few seconds of animation usually fits, often at a smaller size in pixels. Every frame keeps its own timing, the loop setting is kept, and see-through areas stay see-through.

The steps go from gentlest to strongest: lossy compression at full size, then fewer colours and fewer pixels, and as a last resort dropping every other frame. We keep the first step that fits, so the file is as good as 1 MB allows.
tips: Check the result at the size it will be shown. A GIF made smaller in pixels can look fine in a chat window and soft when enlarged.
Screen recordings shrink much better than camera footage, because little changes from one frame to the next.
A GIF already under 1 MB is only cleaned up without visible changes; nothing is made worse to save a few more KB.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 2 MB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 2 MB for websites, docs and messages. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: A GIF made from a screen recording or a video clip is often 5 to 20 MB. To reach 2 MB it is compressed and made smaller in pixels as far as needed, and frames are dropped only as a last resort.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 2 MB
paragraphs: The first lossy step adds a little grain that is hard to see in motion. If that is not enough, the GIF uses fewer colours and fewer pixels, a step at a time, and we keep the first step that fits. Dropping frames comes last, after the pixel size.
The GIF is never converted to a video or another format. It comes back as a GIF, with its frame delays and loop count as they were.
tips: For a GIF in documentation or a README, crop away empty parts of the screen before recording. Pixels you do not record cost nothing.
Lower the frame rate in your screen recorder if you can: 10 to 15 frames a second is usually smooth enough for a demo.
If one GIF has to carry a long demo, splitting it into two shorter GIFs keeps both sharper.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 5 MB
pages.description: Shrink an animated GIF to under 5 MB, keeping its size and every frame where possible. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: Long screen recordings and high-resolution clips saved as GIF can reach 20 to 50 MB. They are compressed to the largest file under 5 MB, still a GIF, with every frame kept wherever the size allows.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 5 MB
paragraphs: Lossy compression comes first: it lets each frame differ very slightly from the original in return for a much smaller file, which is hard to notice while the GIF plays. Clips cut from video usually also need fewer pixels to reach 5 MB.
Very long or very large GIFs can still need fewer pixels. A GIF of many hundreds of frames at full HD is a lot of pictures. If frames had to be dropped, the result says so.
tips: If the GIF came from a video converter, check its frame rate. 30 or more frames a second makes a GIF large; 15 to 20 looks almost the same.
GIFs over 200 million pixels across all frames are refused rather than left running for minutes. Trim or shrink them first.
A GIF already under 5 MB is only cleaned up, losslessly.

pages.heading: Compress a GIF to 10 MB
pages.description: Shrink a large animated GIF to under 10 MB with the gentlest compression that fits. Still animated. Best quality that fits. Free, no sign-up, files deleted minutes after.
pages.blurb: A GIF over 10 MB is usually a long or high-resolution clip. It is cleaned up, then compressed, and made smaller in pixels only as far as 10 MB needs.

guide.title: Getting a GIF under 10 MB
paragraphs: Many large GIFs are bigger than they need to be: GIF makers often store each frame in full when only part of the picture changed. The first step rewrites each frame as only what changed, which changes nothing you can see and is sometimes enough on its own.
If not, gentle lossy compression follows, still at full size and with every frame. Fewer pixels or dropped frames come only after that, and only if 10 MB needs them.
tips: The original is deleted minutes after compression, and the result shortly after, so download it straight away.
Upload limits apply to the file you upload, so check the size shown on the result before you post it.
For a GIF far over 10 MB, like 50 MB or more, a shorter clip will keep more quality than squeezing the whole one.

faq.q: Is it free?
faq.a: Yes. There is no sign-up and no watermark.

faq.q: What happens to my file?
faq.a: It is processed on our server and deleted automatically: the original 5 minutes after the run finishes, the compressed file after 10. A file you upload but never compress is deleted within 30 minutes. You can also delete everything right away with Delete now.

faq.q: Will it look worse?
faq.a: We try a lossless cleanup first, which does not change how the file looks. Only if that is not enough do we lower image quality, and we pick the gentlest setting that still fits your size.

faq.q: What if my file cannot get that small?
faq.a: You get the smallest version we could make and a clear note saying so, instead of a file that silently misses the limit.

faq.q: Why is my file a little under the limit I picked?
faq.a: Some sites count a kilobyte as 1000 bytes and others as 1024. We aim under the stricter one, so a 200 KB page aims for 200,000 bytes and the file passes either way.
